base:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create ONE high-fidelity desktop UI design concept for Intelligence's agent profile editor, a complete single 1920x1080 landscape screenshot. The supplied screenshot is a STYLE AND APP SHELL REFERENCE ONLY, not an instruction to retain its layout.
Keep the familiar calm Day theme: warm ivory canvas, opaque white cards, thin pale neutral borders, muted forest-green primary buttons and star controls, restrained rounding, readable Inter-like sans typography. Preserve the left Intelligence navigation and compact top toolbar from the reference; main content begins to its right. Existing metallic triquetra avatar is the agent's image, not a human. Keep recognizable Intelligence branding. No browser address bar, no design annotations or device frame.
User request: all main profile controls must fit fully in the visible 1920x1080 screen with NO PAGE SCROLLING. Prioritize large clearly visible agent image, editable agent name, spacious editable system prompt, all four rating rows with usable star buttons. Tools and connections must be easy to find and access. Do NOT render User context, Preferred name, or the sharing/settings explanatory block from the old screen anywhere.
Essential content: header Agent profile with Agent Profiles, Resource access, Save profile actions. Name field value Intelligence. Avatar with Change image button. Label the large prompt area System prompt with secondary label Personality & preferences; sample text: You are a thoughtful, practical companion. Explain clearly, stay curious, and help the user learn at their own pace. Help the user accomplish their request with available tools. Verify the outcome of actions. Be honest about uncertainty and tool limitations. Under editor: Internal app instructions remain active.
Default model controls: Uses global model switch, Provider Ollama, Choose model button, Model ID field.
Your ratings section must have EXACTLY these four rows, each with 0 clear button and five stars: Intelligence, Knowledge, Tool-use, Long Tasks. Use illustrative ratings 4,4,3,4; calculated Agent Performance 3.8 / 5, labelled Your assessment. Do not invent benchmarks.
Tools and connections: accessible categories Computer access (Use global computer access), Search, Projects, Calendar, Reports toggles; More tool categories, Skills, MCP servers, Create reusable skills. A compact summary with Manage tools button is acceptable only if variant specifies an overlay approach. Native access restrictions remain app controlled.
Maintain consistent realistic content across variants. Readable real UI text and practical spacing, no large empty wasted areas. Entire profile and bottom of every main card must visibly fit within screenshot.

variants.name: a-balanced-workspace
variants.layout: A — Balanced workspace. Three deliberately unequal columns under a compact title row: left 300px identity card with large avatar, Change image and Name, then a compact Default model card below; middle widest 730px System prompt card with generously tall editor; right 430px Your ratings card above an ALWAYS OPEN compact Tools and connections card with common toggle controls and Skills / MCP rows. Tool controls and all ratings visible simultaneously. Balanced practical composition; prompt is dominant.

variants.name: b-identity-header
variants.layout: B — Identity header. A broad horizontal identity card at top of content holds large avatar at left, editable agent name center-left, compact default model controls to its right. Below, a very wide System prompt panel takes roughly 65% width and Your ratings panel takes 35%. At bottom, a shallow full-width ALWAYS VISIBLE Tools and connections strip with computer scope selector, Search/Projects/Calendar/Reports toggles and Skills/MCP/More tool categories buttons. Four horizontal zones in main canvas, all fully on screen. This is clearly different from any three-column design.

variants.name: c-prompt-first
variants.layout: C — Prompt first. A narrow profile rail at left of main canvas contains image, Change image, Name and Default model. Remaining main area has an extra-wide large System prompt editor at top, with Your ratings as a HORIZONTAL band below it: four compact clearly labelled mini-columns, one for each category, each with clear 0 and five clickable stars; Agent Performance summary aligned at right of same band. Tools and connections is a strong labelled button next to Resource access in the profile header, with a small visible summary of categories enabled near the rail. No overlay open in this screenshot: preserve full visibility of name/avatar/prompt/four ratings. Plenty of prompt writing room, everything fits.

variants.name: d-tools-workbench
variants.layout: D — Tools workbench. Two main columns in canvas, about 70% / 30%. Wide left workspace: compact identity row with large avatar and Name, large System prompt editor immediately beneath, then a full-width horizontal Your ratings band with four groups and performance summary at bottom of left column. Right is a permanent tall Tools and connections inspector, fully expanded with grouped Computer access, 2x2 toggle rows Search/Projects/Calendar/Reports, More tool categories, Skills, MCP servers, Create reusable skills. Compact Default model controls at top of right inspector. No tabs hiding ratings or prompt. All main controls visible at once.

variants.name: e-profile-scorecard
variants.layout: E — Profile scorecard. A distinctive two-column design: left 470px tall profile card combines large centered avatar, Change image, Name, then Your ratings with four generous horizontal label-plus-stars rows and Agent Performance at bottom. Right wide editorial workspace contains large System prompt editor in top two-thirds; beneath it two side-by-side shallow cards: Default model with compact controls on left, Tools and connections summary on right with clear Manage tools button and labelled Skills/MCP/Computer access entries. Tool access is one click to a focused modal, shown CLOSED, so profile stays entirely visible. Header contains Resource access and Save profile. Avoid looking like A: identity and ratings are unified in one left card; prompt dominates right.
